output.summary: Approved the G1018 design (attempt 2). A checkpoint input selected by change or tree renders the producer's full checkpoint view (commit, base, change, diff, plus tree only when tree is the selected field), guarded so it never shows a mismatched commit, and with no fingerprint change. The approve items name commit and base. shrink is reworked: views are never blobbed, argv duplication is dropped, previews are clipped, blobbed dicts get key summaries, and shrink never grows a card. 4 KB is an explicit target with structural guarantees G1-G3 tested. Bounding `previous` is deferred to G1019. The reviewer's four implementation notes go to implement. Decision made by Claude (root agent) under the owner's standing delegation for Release 1.

responses.review_design:1:1: fixed: Measured with a replay of shrink that reproduces card-1014-implement at exactly 4,621 bytes (it also showed shrink grows that card from 4,219: blob views are larger than the instruction texts they replace). Checkpoint views are now never shrink candidates; shrink first drops argv (keeps command), dedupes context.commands vs commands_to_run, clips blob summaries to 120 chars, then blobs largest-first only when that reduces size; blobbed dicts get a key summary; tree is dropped unless selected. Real-size results: implement 3,745, review_impl 3,765 with both views inline, review_tests 3,829; all 38 replayed cards without `previous` are <= 4,096. Explicit decision: 4,096 is a target. Guaranteed and tested: views never blobbed, shrink never grows a card, result is <= 4,096 or shrink is exhausted (idempotent, no reducing candidate), and real-size implement/review_tests/review_impl fixtures are <= 4,096. The journey test asserts the exhaustion property instead of a bare 4,096 bound; the bare-40-hex check is limited to top-level inputs/context values (reviewer's minor note). Bounding `previous` (the only reason cards stay over) is out of scope and proposed as a child goal after G1000.

output.summary: Sub-field checkpoint selectors (`.change`, `.tree`) render {commit, base, change, diff} (tree only when selected) through the same source resolve used, with an equality guard and bare-value fallback; approve items gain commit and base; fingerprints are untouched. shrink never blobs a checkpoint view, never grows a card, and first recovers truly redundant bytes (argv duplicates, duplicated commands list, 120-char blob previews, correction full.summary), with a key summary instead of `{` for blobbed dicts. Replayed on all 38 real 54d7e83 cards: implement 4,621 -> 3,745 and review_impl 3,765 with both views inline; every card without `previous` fits 4,096. Decision: 4,096 is a target, not a hard limit; tests assert the guaranteed properties plus a measured real-size bound, and bounding `previous` is proposed as a follow-up goal after G1000.

findings.text: F1 Card size budget does not hold. At 54d7e83 the real implement card (card-1014-implement) is 4,621 canonical bytes after shrink has already blobbed the prompt and all instructions. shrink stops and returns an oversized card (test_card_shape_and_size already allows 4096+2000). A sub-field checkpoint view adds about 303 bytes, so shrink immediately blobs it into {summary:'{', blob, read}, which shows less than today's bare id. review_impl (3 instruction blobs, doc, checks, two views) works out to about 4.7 KB, so both views get blobbed. Consequence: the spec acceptance (review_impl carries commit/base/diff) fails on real cards, and the design's journey test either fails or passes only on fixture-sized cards. Fix: exempt checkpoint views from shrink (or blob them last) and recover space elsewhere (truncate artifact summaries, which shrink never touches today; drop duplicate argv/command forms), optionally drop tree when tree is not the selected sub-field, give blob_view a useful summary, and state the budget with measured real-size implement/review_impl cards, or record an explicit limit decision and test the actual bound.

output.summary: Approved. F1 resolved: replay reproduced (implement 3,745, review_impl 3,765 synthesized and 3,973 on the real review_impl-z card with both views inline, every card without `previous` <= 4,096); G2 and idempotence hold on all 42 run cards; '4,096 is a target' is stated and G1-G3 are tested; the shrink steps keep runnable `command` strings and useful blob summaries; no function overlap with G1016 or G1000. Four non-blocking implementation notes in the artifact.

spec:
Bug found while dogfooding Release 1. The default graph binds code inputs by sub-field so that fingerprints follow the right identity: review_tests, implement and review_impl take `test_design.tests.change`; review_impl and approve_merge take `implement.code.change`; run_tests and integrate take `implement.code.tree`. But card.value_of renders `checkpoint_view` (commit, base, tree, change, diff command) only when the selector has no path. These cards therefore show a bare patch id or tree id, which is not a commit and cannot be diffed. The G1014 review_tests reviewer could not locate the tests and had to dig the commit out of goal.json. Every code review and the merge approval would be equally blind. Approve items (render.py) may have the same gap: check.

Outcome:
- A card input whose selector names a checkpoint output plus a sub-field (`change` or `tree`) renders the full checkpoint view of that output, so the reviewer gets the commit and the diff command. The fingerprint still uses only the selected sub-field. Rendering must not change any input fingerprint.
- Human approve items show the same commit and diff.
- The card size budget (4 KB) still holds.

Acceptance:
- Engine tests: a review_tests card and a review_impl card each carry commit, base and diff for their tests and code inputs, and the diff command runs and shows the goal's own changes.
- The approve_merge item shows the code commit.
- Fingerprints of the affected nodes are unchanged before and after the fix, so no in-flight goal goes stale.
- The renamed-graph variant passes.
- A regression test reads each agent card of a full journey and checks that every checkpoint-typed input carries a commit that `git cat-file -t` resolves to a commit.
title: Show the full checkpoint on cards for inputs selected by change or tree
